Sometimes people bring friends and it is never a big deal and we all celebrate a great man. This year, we had 3 of the 4 of my mother-in-law’s kids and their families come and had a wonderful time. This can be especially true if you have a mentor or role model within the group who can offer guidance and support. 4. **Accountability and encouragement**: A values-based community can provide a sense of accountability, where individuals feel motivated to live up to the expectations of their peers. This can be a powerful driver of personal growth, as individuals strive to meet the standards set by their community. 5. **Flexibility and autonomy**: Unlike a religious community, a values-based community may offer more flexibility and autonomy, allowing individuals to explore their own spirituality and values without feeling bound by dogma or doctrine. However, it's worth noting that a values-based community may not provide the same level of structure and guidance as a religious community. Without a clear set of rules or teachings, individuals may need to take more responsibility for their own personal growth and development. Ultimately, whether a values-based community can push people to be better in the same way a religious community does depends on the specific individuals involved and the values they share.
